THESIS_TITLE: Development of a Web Interface for a Human–Robot Workplace
THESIS_SUMMARY: My master's thesis investigated how user-configurable multimodal feedback can support transparency, usability, and interaction in collaborative human–robot work environments.
THESIS_POINT_1: Designed and developed a configurable web-based interface for multimodal feedback in collaborative robotic assembly environments.
THESIS_POINT_2: Conducted a two-phase empirical user study investigating transparency, usability, cognitive workload, and user-driven configuration behavior.
THESIS_POINT_3: Collected and analyzed questionnaire responses, interaction logs, and user behavior using descriptive statistics and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
THESIS_POINT_4: Evaluated configurable software behavior and user interaction patterns in collaborative software systems through empirical analysis.
THESIS_POINT_5: Integrated web-based frontend systems with ROS-based robotic infrastructure through REST APIs and runtime reconfiguration mechanisms.
